Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage is dominated by two intertwined AI-industry storylines: Anthropic's roadshow for what could be one of the largest IPOs in history, and the spiraling Nvidia scandal over CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman U.S. officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset. Alongside that, outlets are closely tracking hot inflation data that has revived fears of a December Fed rate hike, along with CoreWeave's earnings-driven AI stock rally and simmering Strait of Hormuz tensions between the U.S. and Iran.

stories.headline: Anthropic sets IPO range valuing it at up to $1.4 trillion amid AI stock sell-off
stories.summary: Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow with a price range of $70-$78 a share, implying a valuation well short of the roughly $2 trillion once floated, as seven tech partners including Google and Nvidia agreed to buy $26 billion of stock alongside the offering. The debut, expected to price November 18 and begin trading November 19, lands amid an AI stock sell-off following the midterms and the Nvidia spy scandal.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy roils company and AI industry
stories.summary: Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive U.S. intelligence believes was a Chinese intelligence asset, has triggered an independent Nvidia board investigation, wiped out over $1 trillion in market value, and shaken Taiwan's view of its most famous tech figure. Congress has demanded a briefing and Morgan Stanley pulled Nvidia from its top picks list, citing Huang's leadership as "crucial" even as scrutiny mounts.

stories.headline: Hot October inflation report cements expectations for a December Fed rate hike
stories.summary: Fed governor Christopher Waller said the central bank may need to raise rates by a half-point in December, double the usual move, after core CPI data showed inflation remaining stubbornly hot for a third straight month. Axios reported that bond yields and Fed officials including Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan are increasingly leaning toward a larger or faster series of hikes.

stories.headline: CoreWeave results reignite AI trade, lifting Nasdaq and tech stocks broadly
stories.summary: CoreWeave shares jumped roughly 25% after reassuring quarterly results, helping push the Nasdaq up about 2% and re-energizing a battered AI trade following last week's sharp sell-off. FT noted the rally also erased the prior week's losses as hopes rose for a higher Anthropic IPO valuation.

stories.headline: U.S. and Iran exchange strikes over control of the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The U.S. and Iran have struck islands in the waterway in a fierce battle for control of the strait, with Adnoc Gas now examining options including a new LNG export facility to bypass reliance on the chokepoint entirely.

stories.headline: Senior U.S. Army soldier arrested in U.K. on suspicion of spying for Russia
stories.summary: A 41-year-old U.S. soldier assigned to a NATO rapid reaction command in the U.K. was arrested by British police over allegations of spying for Russia, in an investigation involving the FBI and American military. FT reported the probe is being led by British Counter Terrorism Policing.

stories.headline: Marvell's $115 billion bid for Lumentum faces lukewarm investor reception
stories.summary: Marvell Technology's plan to deepen its AI bet through a roughly $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum Holdings is drawing skepticism from investors, with odds on the deal closing described as close to a coin flip.

stories.headline: H&R REIT's $4.7 billion breakup faces shareholder revolt
stories.summary: H&R Real Estate Investment Trust's C$6.7 billion breakup plan is facing growing opposition from major shareholders, including some of the world's largest pension funds.

Business.gaps: No recent business-relevant items found from Puck or Business Insider in this window; Politico's feed items were largely political/2028-focused rather than business-news leads.

US politics.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from Congress's return after Democrats' midterm landslide: a blocked Hegseth impeachment push, new House and Senate GOP minority leadership, and an emerging rift among Senate Democrats over who should lead them in the majority. Outlets are also closely tracking early 2028 positioning (Rubio, Vance), White House warnings to incoming Democratic investigators, and lingering Biden 2024 fallout.

stories.headline: House GOP blocks Hegseth impeachment effort
stories.summary: House Republicans voted 211-204 to send Rep. Thomas Massie's impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth back to committee, with Massie the lone GOP 'no' vote, though Democrats are expected to revive the push once they control Congress in January.

stories.headline: Jim Jordan elected House GOP minority leader as Thune set to lead Senate Republicans
stories.summary: House Republicans elected Jim Jordan over Steve Scalise as incoming minority leader for the 120th Congress following their midterm losses, while John Thune was chosen to lead Senate Republicans in the minority.

stories.headline: Rift grows among Senate Democrats over who leads in the majority
stories.summary: Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin publicly said they will not back Chuck Schumer to remain Senate leader, exposing a growing divide among Democrats as they prepare to take the majority.

stories.headline: White House warns incoming Democratic majority against aggressive oversight
stories.summary: As Rep. Robert Garcia prepares to lead the House Oversight Committee, White House counsel has pushed back on planned investigations, with Courthouse News noting Garcia stressed Congress's powers don't need the 'permission of the White House.'

stories.headline: 'Draft Marco' movement grows as Republicans eye a wide-open 2028
stories.summary: Politico reports growing numbers of Hill Republicans are rallying behind Marco Rubio for 2028 as the party reassesses its bench after the midterm defeat, a dynamic also explored by The Dispatch's look at JD Vance's own positioning.

stories.headline: Massie forces another Epstein files vote
stories.summary: Rep. Thomas Massie is forcing a new House floor vote on legislation to release files related to the Jeffrey Epstein case, continuing a recurring fight over transparency.

stories.headline: Biden says he wouldn't have run in 2024 if he'd known about his cancer
stories.summary: In an interview with People magazine, the former president said he would not have sought reelection had he known of his cancer diagnosis, and called his widely panned June 2024 debate performance 'not very consequential'—a claim Fox News said drew sharp criticism.

stories.headline: Kennedy family sues to block Trump's Arlington arch
stories.summary: Nine members of the Kennedy family have joined a lawsuit arguing that President Trump's planned D.C. arch near Arlington National Cemetery would disrupt views and cast shadows over the graves of their ancestors, including JFK.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS and Cook Political Report had no current (last 24-48h) items surfaced in search; results for those outlets were mostly weeks or months old. Politico, NYT, WSJ, and The Guardian were covered only via provided feed items since they block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative, alongside a wave of blockbuster AI financial news: Anthropic's historic IPO roadshow, OpenAI crossing $10 billion in quarterly revenue, and CoreWeave's earnings reviving the broader AI trade. Secondary threads include new AI model and research releases (DeepMind, Anthropic), AI chip supply-chain deals (TSMC), and EU regulatory moves against tech platforms.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang faces Congress over alleged Chinese spy affair
stories.summary: House Republicans gave Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang until Wednesday to agree to a closed-door briefing on his relationship with a woman U.S. officials believe was a Chinese intelligence asset, as Nvidia's board launches its own investigation and roughly 240,000 banned chips are reported to have reached China through a company tied to her. The scandal is straining Taiwan's pride in its most famous tech executive and has split Silicon Valley, with some allies like Elon Musk defending Huang as the subject of a personal lapse rather than a security failure.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches IPO roadshow, could be valued above $1.4 trillion
stories.summary: Anthropic, in a company announcement, said it launched the roadshow for its IPO, offering 825 million Class A shares with plans to list on Nasdaq under ticker "ANT," with bankers reportedly now weighing pushing the valuation above the initial $1.4 trillion target amid oversubscribed demand. TechCrunch reported the firm set a price range of $70-$78 a share, a deal that would also see $26 billion in shares sold privately to chipmakers and cloud partners including Nvidia and Google.

stories.headline: OpenAI's quarterly revenue tops $10 billion for the first time
stories.summary: OpenAI told investors its revenue jumped nearly 50% to about $10 billion in the third quarter, up sharply from $6.7 billion the prior quarter, though the company continues to post heavy losses even as it still trails Anthropic on some growth metrics according to The Decoder.

stories.headline: CoreWeave's earnings reignite the AI trade on Wall Street
stories.summary: CoreWeave is leaning on customer prepayments, contract-backed borrowing, and shorter-term deals to fund its AI buildout, a shift disclosed alongside third-quarter results that sent its shares surging and helped lift the Nasdaq as investors bet the AI boom still has room to run.

stories.headline: TSMC to invest $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI
stories.summary: Taiwan's TSMC is putting $1 billion into both Anthropic and OpenAI, the latest instance of the AI industry's circular financing arrangements even as the broader AI trade has been wobbling.

stories.headline: DeepMind's AI mathematically verifies Signal's encryption core in weeks, not years
stories.summary: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code system formally verified key parts of Signal's cryptographic core in a four-week project, a task that traditionally takes years, with AI agents reportedly writing more than six million lines toward the proof — a signal that AI could make formal verification far more practical.

stories.headline: EU's new Digital Fairness Act targets loot boxes, influencers and 'dark patterns'
stories.summary: Brussels has proposed a sweeping Digital Fairness Act aimed at gaming, social media and e-commerce platforms, with Wired reporting that companies like Duolingo, Strava and Ticketmaster are caught up in rules that would force disclosure of paid influencer content and limit manipulative engagement features.

stories.headline: Chinese AI startups try to poach Silicon Valley's top AI talent
stories.summary: Rest of World reports that Chinese AI firms like MiniMax and Moonshot are setting up U.S. outposts to recruit talent away from OpenAI and Anthropic, though steep pay gaps, weaker prestige, and national-security tensions make the effort an uphill climb.

Tech & AI.gaps: VentureBeat and IEEE Spectrum yielded no distinct recent AI/tech leads beyond older or tangential items; The Information, Platformer, and Anthropic/DeepMind coverage above reflects only what surfaced in web search since these sites are partially paywalled.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging heavily on COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, with Carbon Brief leading detailed data analysis on finance pledges and delegate counts, while Heatmap digs into the U.S. permitting reform bill (BAAJA) and its post-midterm political momentum. Separately, wire and business outlets are tracking winter energy costs, nuclear fuel markets, and Gulf oil infrastructure risk tied to the Strait of Hormuz, and utility-focused trades are dissecting how last week's U.S. midterm results are reshaping data-center and ratepayer politics.

stories.headline: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's analysis finds that public funding pledged to help developing countries tackle climate change has dropped sharply as the COP31 summit convenes in Antalya, Turkey, raising questions about financing commitments amid a record delegate turnout.

stories.headline: Martin Heinrich on the path forward for the bipartisan permitting bill
stories.summary: Heatmap's exclusive interview with Senator Martin Heinrich covers his push to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act now, arguing the bill would finally create a one-stop federal process for approving major power lines and help lock in decarbonization gains in the electricity sector.

stories.headline: Winter heating costs set to rise 7%, with heating oil up 70%
stories.summary: The New York Times reports that U.S. households face average winter heating bill increases of 7%, with heating-oil users facing roughly 70% higher costs because the war involving Iran has sharply reduced supply of that fuel.

stories.headline: Nuclear revival pushes CME to advance physical uranium futures contract
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that the nuclear power boom is prompting CME Group to move ahead with a new futures contract backed by physical supplies of uranium, a key reactor fuel source.

stories.headline: Adnoc Gas still evaluating ways to bypass the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: WSJ reports that Adnoc Gas's chief executive says the company is examining ways to reduce reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, including a potential LNG export facility on the UAE's east coast.

stories.headline: Midterm sweep sends shockwaves through energy and utility policy
stories.summary: Latitude Media's post-election coverage argues that Democratic midterm upsets in Texas, Ohio and Wisconsin will trigger an abrupt shift in energy and data-center policy, with separate pieces noting voters in Georgia and Michigan punishing utility monopolies over rate hikes.

stories.headline: Fossil-fuel CO2 emissions projected to dip slightly in 2026 as Iran conflict curbs oil use
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's analysis projects global CO2 emissions from fossil fuels and cement will fall by about 0.4% in 2026 to 38.2 billion tonnes, partly due to reduced oil use linked to the Iran conflict.

stories.headline: FERC commissioner LaCerte on midterms, PJM and utility affordability
stories.summary: Utility Dive reports FERC Commissioner David LaCerte linking the affordability crisis to insufficient infrastructure build-out, commenting on PJM dynamics and utility monopoly concerns in the wake of recent elections.

Energy.gaps: No recent (last 24-48h) original reporting could be found via search for Canary Media, E&E News, or Argus Media; their search results returned only older or evergreen/about pages rather than current news.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage this week is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair and the related 'Chinese spy' allegations, alongside intensive diplomatic groundwork for next week's Trump-Xi summit at APEC in Shenzhen. Business outlets are also tracking strong Chinese export and EV data, major Chinese tech product launches (Alibaba, Huawei), and tensions over Hong Kong infrastructure costs and Taiwan-mainland travel friction.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair fuels 'Chinese spy' scandal and Washington backlash
stories.summary: Nvidia's board launched an investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a woman identified in reports as a suspected Chinese intelligence asset tied to Singapore-based chip buyer Megaspeed, triggering a stock drop and renewed congressional scrutiny of Nvidia's China chip sales. State-run Global Times dismissed the spy claims as a 'groundless smear' and accused US media of a 'presumption of guilt' against Chinese Americans, while Taiwan's WSJ coverage says the episode has strained Huang's standing as the island's hometown tech hero.

stories.headline: Rubio and Wang Yi finalize preparations for Trump-Xi summit at APEC Shenzhen
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke by phone with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi to finalize arrangements for next week's Trump-Xi meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, as both sides seek to keep a fragile trade truce intact. China's commerce ministry separately voiced 'serious concern' over fresh US sanctions on two Chinese firms just days before the leaders meet.

stories.headline: China's exports jump 35.2% in October on surging AI-chip trade
stories.summary: Caixin reports that China's overseas shipments rose 35.2% in October, beating forecasts, with the gain driven more by higher prices than larger volumes as computing equipment and chips surged in value.

stories.headline: China's NEV sales hit record 1.94 million in October even as overall car market slows
stories.summary: CAAM data cited by CnEVPost shows battery-electric vehicle sales reached a record 1.353 million units in October, up 22% year-on-year, pushing overall NEV sales to a record 1.94 million even as broader passenger car demand weakens.

stories.headline: Outcry after Taiwan asks mainland Chinese tourist to sign independence statement
stories.summary: A mainland Chinese tourist was asked to sign a declaration recognising Taiwan as an independent state in order to obtain an entry permit, sparking controversy over Taipei's entry requirements just as cross-strait tensions remain elevated ahead of Taiwan's local elections.

stories.headline: Alibaba opens Qwen4-Max preview and discloses Hong Kong IPO filing for chip unit T-Head
stories.summary: Alibaba opened a preview of its flagship Qwen4-Max AI model, which supports image and video inputs and a million-token context window, while separately confirming that its chip unit T-Head has been cleared to proceed with a Hong Kong listing after a September filing.

stories.headline: Hong Kong cuts Northern Link railway budget by 28% using mainland-referenced standards
stories.summary: A new railway line meant to anchor an infrastructure megaproject strengthening Hong Kong's ties with neighbouring mainland cities will now cost about HK$86.2 billion, down more than a quarter from earlier estimates, after officials applied mainland-referenced construction standards.

stories.headline: China's State Council moves to stabilize capital markets and speed overdue business payments
stories.summary: China's State Council, chaired by Premier Li Qiang, called for stronger mechanisms to stabilize capital markets and directed authorities to ensure full, prompt payment of debts owed to businesses, while regulators separately cracked down on AI-generated celebrity impersonation scams.

China.gaps: Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, and Yicai Global had no recent China-politics/economy coverage surfaced in search; CGTN and China Daily yielded no distinct recent stories beyond general Xi-Trump summit framing already covered via Xinhua.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by the intensifying US-Iran conflict over the Strait of Hormuz, alongside deepening humanitarian crises in Gaza and Lebanon and fast-moving Israeli political maneuvering after the recent election. Gulf business outlets are separately tracking how Wall Street firms and regional governments are repositioning capital amid war-related economic uncertainty.

stories.headline: Iran escalates attacks on shipping and infrastructure in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran struck ship navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island and an oil tanker reportedly hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, part of a pattern of attacks that has disrupted Gulf oil flows despite ongoing diplomacy to end the war. The G7 separately condemned Iran's obstruction of the waterway and demanded it stop attacking civilian vessels.

stories.headline: Trump vows 'total victory' against Iran, predicts decades-long recovery
stories.summary: President Trump declared that Iran has waged war on the US since 1979 and said Washington needs a complete victory, while separately claiming Tehran would need 25 years to recover from American strikes. His remarks came as Iran's security chief threatened to strike US bases in Europe if Washington resumes attacks.

stories.headline: Gaza floods compound humanitarian crisis as aid delays draw UN criticism
stories.summary: UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher said waiting for a new Israeli government to form is not an acceptable reason to delay winter aid into Gaza, after heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents and killed several people including children. Netanyahu's office has blamed Hamas for the suffering, while Israeli figures show aid entry has declined since January.

stories.headline: Houthis and Saudi-led coalition trade attacks as Yemen fighting intensifies
stories.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles as explosions were heard in Aden, while the WHO reported casualties from renewed Yemen fighting have surged to nearly 12,000. G7 foreign ministers issued a joint statement condemning continued Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and urging Iran to stop arming the group.

stories.headline: Eisenkot consolidates power in Knesset but urges caution on Iran
stories.summary: Former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot said Israel should not return to war with Iran for now, even as his political bloc secured key Knesset committee posts and effectively took control of parliament's arrangements. Eisenkot has also demanded regular security briefings from Netanyahu during the caretaker government period.

stories.headline: Apollo takes stake in Mubadala Capital as Wall Street deepens Gulf ties
stories.summary: Apollo Global Management has acquired a minority stake in Abu Dhabi's Mubadala Capital, a deal expected to support the Emirati fund's global expansion and reflecting how major Wall Street firms are shifting from fundraising with Gulf investors to forming long-term strategic partnerships. Apollo's CEO also forecast roughly $1 trillion in Gulf spending on infrastructure and trade diversification following the Iran war.

stories.headline: More than a million people in Lebanon face acute food insecurity, UN warns
stories.summary: The UN has warned that a hunger crisis affecting almost a quarter of Lebanon's population could worsen without urgent intervention. The warning adds to mounting regional economic strain tied to the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.headline: Oman's economy outpaces Gulf neighbours despite war-related investment risks
stories.summary: Higher oil prices and rising hydrocarbon exports have helped Oman's economy and stock market outperform regional peers this year, as its ports outside the Strait of Hormuz attracted trade diverted from the blockaded waterway. Analysts caution that the US-Iran war could still curb foreign direct investment across the wider Gulf going forward.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not verify recent coverage from Gulf News, Khaleej Times, Arabian Business, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, Ynetnews, Haaretz, or Al-Monitor beyond items already found via search or feed; Reuters, AP, FT, The Economist were not searchable and had no relevant feed items provided.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: African outlets are converging on Dangote's refinery IPO and upstream expansion, DRC's contentious referendum law fueling third-term fears for President Tshisekedi, and Nigeria's run-up to 2027 elections including a major voter-roll purge. Climate (COP31), US-Africa security and trade tensions (Madagascar-Russia ties, South Africa's AGOA exclusion), and steady mining-sector investment activity round out the agenda.

stories.headline: DR Congo: Tshisekedi signs new referendum law amid third-term fears
stories.summary: President Felix Tshisekedi has signed a law easing the rules for holding constitutional referendums, prompting concern he may be laying groundwork to extend his rule beyond term limits. Africa Confidential has separately reported on Tshisekedi's moves toward a 'national conversation' and constitutional changes that critics say could produce a third term.

stories.headline: Dangote pushes $30bn upstream expansion as refinery IPO draws heavy demand
stories.summary: Aliko Dangote says he has the financial firepower to become a major Nigerian oil producer as he presses ahead with plans to spend more than $30bn expanding his refining empire, while Africa Confidential reports his refinery's $1.6bn IPO drew nearly triple demand from investors ahead of a planned November listing. TechCabal's daily briefing also noted Dangote Cement has abandoned a planned London listing.

stories.headline: World leaders face pressure to act at COP31 as climate warnings intensify
stories.summary: World leaders are gathering in Turkey for COP31 amid mounting pressure for urgent climate action, a summit African Business says must 'deliver, not just convene' for African negotiators pressing for climate finance.

stories.headline: US warns Madagascar over growing security ties with Russia
stories.summary: A deputy head of US Africa Command warned that Madagascar's deepening military cooperation with Moscow mirrors partnerships with military-led African governments that have failed to improve security.

stories.headline: Nigeria 2027: INEC removes 1.6 million names from voter register
stories.summary: Just over two months before Nigeria's general elections, the electoral commission says it has purged more than 1.6 million irregular voter records and flagged at least 54 staff members suspected of manipulating the register.

stories.headline: African mining sector poised for investment growth despite bankability risks
stories.summary: Mining Weekly reports African mining is positioned to attract increased investment over the next three to five years on the back of geopolitical shifts and critical-mineral demand, even as a shortage of bankable projects poses a challenge; separately, Barrick's copper mill expansion in Zambia is nearing completion on schedule.

stories.headline: US courts South Africa despite AGOA and G20 exclusions
stories.summary: Departments within the Trump administration and major US tech firms including Amazon, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Microsoft, SpaceX and Zipline are courting Cape Town's tech sector even as Washington has excluded South Africa from AGOA and the G20.

stories.headline: Algeria sentences writer Kamel Daoud to five years over novel
stories.summary: An Algerian court sentenced award-winning writer Kamel Daoud and his wife to five years in prison, in absentia, over allegations of breaching medical confidentiality and invading privacy tied to one of his novels.

Africa.gaps: The Continent: only older archived issues were found via search, nothing from the last 48 hours could be confirmed. Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so their current Africa coverage could not be verified.

Media.overview: Coverage clusters around AI's collision with journalism economics (a possible blockbuster NYT-OpenAI settlement), cost pressures reshaping legacy broadcast news (ABC and CBS), and the slow erosion of local news infrastructure worldwide, from Canada's funding renewal to the near-disappearance of UK news agencies. A journalist's killing in Ecuador also underscores global press-freedom risks, while Puck highlights how legacy broadcasters like NBC are still winning the fight for digital election-night attention against creators.

stories.headline: What Could the Times Buy With Its A.I. Bucks?
stories.summary: Puck reports legal experts expect OpenAI and Microsoft to settle the New York Times' copyright lawsuit for well over a billion dollars after a November 20 briefing deadline, potentially bankrolling further M&A by the Times.

stories.headline: Killing of journalist underscores deteriorating conditions in Ecuador
stories.summary: Reporter Tomás Beltrán was shot dead over the weekend amid gang warfare that has made Ecuador one of Latin America's most violent countries, raising fresh alarm about journalist safety.

stories.headline: ABC's Cost-Cutting Anxiety
stories.summary: Status reports several senior ABC News figures are taking Disney's voluntary early-retirement offers, with remaining staffers anxious about further cuts to come.

stories.headline: “It’s either this or death”: Canada renews the Local Journalism Initiative and extends journalism tax credit
stories.summary: Canada's proposed federal budget extends the journalism tax credit by hundreds of millions of dollars and expands eligibility to audio and audiovisual news, a lifeline for struggling local outlets.

stories.headline: Some local news outlets are losing physical newsrooms
stories.summary: A Northwestern University Local News Initiative report finds that beyond pandemic-driven remote work, many local outlets are now permanently shedding their physical newsroom spaces altogether.

stories.headline: Around 90% of UK local news agencies appear to have closed since the 1980s
stories.summary: Press Gazette finds Britain's once-thriving network of independent news agencies supplying Fleet Street has shrunk to just 17 surviving members from hundreds in previous decades.

stories.headline: Children of the Kornacki
stories.summary: Puck details how NBC's 'Kornacki Cam' livestream drew tens of millions of views across platforms on election night, becoming the go-to feed even for rival streamers and creators, illustrating legacy media's continued pull in the creator era.

Media.gaps: NYT, WSJ, FT and Bloomberg had no media-industry feed items provided and could not be independently searched since those sites block search access.
